title: Simulation of one transition
statement: Let $k,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $x$ be a finite binary input, and let $\mathrm{tr}$ be a transition rule for a machine with $k$ work tapes and states indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. Suppose a configuration $c$ is in state $q$, and let $d$ be a configuration of the machine that simulates one transition, with its state at the entry phase and its work tapes and head positions related to those of $c$ as prescribed by the representation relation. Write $a$ for the action selected by $\mathrm{tr}$ from state $q$, the symbol under the input head of $c$, and the symbols under its work-tape heads. Then there is an integer $T$ with $0<T\le 50(L+1)$, where $L$ is the length of the binary encoding of the transition table, such that after $T$ steps the simulating machine is at the exit phase determined by whether $a$ has a successor state, and its configuration represents the result of applying $a$ to $c$. At every intermediate time $u$ with $0<u<T$, its state is neither the entry nor the halt anchor; its output is unchanged through time $T$. Each original work-tape head visits only its position in $c$ or its position after applying $a$, and each of the two additional work-tape heads visits only positions in the interval $[-50(L+1),50(L+1)]$.
hypotheses_covered: transition rule $\mathrm{tr}$ on the specified state, input-symbol, and work-symbol types
